title_en: Jiangsu Nantong Erjian Group Co., Ltd. v. Wujiang Hengsen Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over a construction project contract
ruling_gist_en: The construction project delivered by the contractor shall meet the delivery conditions agreed in the contract and the relevant project acceptance standards. If the project actually has obvious quality defects, the people's court shall not support the contractor's claim that the project quality is up to standard based on certificates of completion acceptance, etc.
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over construction project contract; Second instance; High People's Court; Jiangsu Province; Legal person; Contract Law; Whether project quality is up to standard; Bearing of repair costs; Liability for construction delay; Partial support; Construction project contract; Roof leakage; Completion acceptance; Construction delay; Contract dispute; Company construction project contract dispute
full_text_en:
Jiangsu Nantong Erjian Group Co., Ltd. v. Wujiang Hengsen Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over construction project construction contract

[Ruling Summary]

A construction project delivered by the contractor shall meet the delivery conditions agreed in the contract and the relevant project acceptance standards. Where the project actually has obvious quality defects, and the contractor claims that the project quality is qualified based on documents such as the project completion acceptance certificate, the People's Court shall not support such claim.

Under circumstances where the trust required for cooperation between the two parties has been lost, to resolve the dispute between them, the People's Court may rule that the developer may commission a third party to rectify the project quality by reference to the repair design plan, and the costs incurred shall be borne by the contractor.

Plaintiff and Counterclaim Defendant: Jiangsu Nantong Erjian Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Renmin Zhonglu, Qidong City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant and Counterclaim Plaintiff: Wujiang Hengsen Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Lize Road, Songling Town, Wujiang City, Jiangsu Province.

Jiangsu Nantong Erjian Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Nantong Erjian) filed a lawsuit with the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province against Wujiang Hengsen Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hengsen Company) regarding the main action for payment of the remaining project款项 and the counterclaim for compensation for losses from redoing the roof leakage repairs under a construction project construction contract dispute. The court rendered the Civil Judgment (2006) Su Zhong Min Yi Chu Zi No. 0022 on August 5, 2010. Both Nantong Erjian and Hengsen Company were dissatisfied and appealed to the Jiangsu High People's Court. The court rendered the Civil Ruling (2010) Su Min Zhong Zi No. 0188 on March 3, 2011, setting aside the original judgment and remanding the case for retrial.

During the retrial, Plaintiff Nantong Erjian alleged: On October 15, 2004, the plaintiff and the defendant entered into a "Construction Project Construction Contract," agreeing that the plaintiff would undertake the civil engineering construction of the Wujiang Hengsen International Plaza. On July 20, 2005, the involved project passed the completion acceptance and was simultaneously received and used by the defendant, Hengsen Company. The defendant only paid RMB 26,815,307 and refused to pay the remaining balance of RMB 16,207,442. The plaintiff requested the court to: 1. Order the defendant to pay the remaining project款项 and liquidated damages for overdue payment of RMB 153,922.39, totaling RMB 16,361,364.39. 2. Order the defendant to compensate the plaintiff for losses of RMB 60,000 due to the scrapping of成型 steel bars caused by design changes.

Defendant Hengsen Company argued: The defendant had paid the project款项 in accordance with the agreed terms, and requested the court to dismiss the claims of the plaintiff, Nantong Erjian. It also filed a counterclaim: 1. The counterclaim defendant cut corners, did not construct according to the design drawings, and the quality was unqualified, resulting in extensive roof leakage. The quotation for redoing this part of the project was RMB 3,335,092.99. The counterclaim defendant should be ordered to compensate for this loss. 2. The project completion date agreed by both parties was mid-April 2005, but the actual completion date was July 26, 2005, a delay of 91.5 days. The counterclaim defendant should pay liquidated damages of RMB 9.15 million for the delay.

Nantong Erjian argued in response to Hengsen Company's counterclaim: 1. The involved project had passed the completion acceptance. For a project that has passed the completion acceptance, the "Regulations on Quality Management of Construction Projects" stipulates that the construction unit only has warranty obligations. 2. The roof leakage was caused by reasons such as the lack of a upturned edge at the expansion joint of the floor slab in the original design. Furthermore, after the project was completed, Hengsen Company's lessee arbitrarily drilled screw holes on the roof to install lights, damaging the waterproof layer. 3. According to the meeting minutes of both parties, Hengsen Company had acknowledged that the delay was caused by various factors including the basement, and explicitly agreed not to pursue the original contract schedule, with no reward or penalty. Therefore, the counterclaim requests were not accepted.

The court of first instance, the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, found the following facts:

On October 15, 2004, Nantong Erjian and Hengsen Company legally entered into a construction project construction contract, which agreed that Nantong Erjian would undertake all civil engineering work of the Wujiang Hengsen International Plaza, which was contracted out by Hengsen Company. The contract price was RMB 30,079,113, the commencement date was October 31, 2004, and the completion date was April 28, 2005. On the same day, the parties signed a supplementary agreement stipulating: the planned commencement date was October 2, 2004 (subject to the commencement order), the completion date was March 11, 2005, and the工期 was 141 days (15 days before and after the Spring Festival not counted). For each day of delay, Nantong Erjian would pay liquidated damages of RMB 100,000. The civil engineering cost was tentatively set at RMB 35.23 million based on the tender base price. After the completion settlement was verified by a qualified audit department of Wujiang City, the total final settlement price would be the audited total price reduced by 9.5%. The supplementary agreement also stipulated the payment method and agreed that 5% of the total price would be retained as a warranty deposit, to be returned after two years.

On October 30, 2004, Nantong Erjian wrote to Hengsen Company, stating that design changes had caused losses from scrapped成型 steel bars of approximately RMB 60,000, and requested Hengsen Company to bear this loss. On November 10, 2004, Hengsen Company replied to Nantong Erjian, stating that成型 steel bars should be utilized as much as possible, and for those truly unusable, Nantong Erjian should submit a detailed list, and after verification by both parties, Hengsen Company would provide compensation. Thereafter, Nantong Erjian did not submit a detailed list of losses.

On January 6, 2005, Nantong Erjian and Hengsen Company signed meeting minutes, confirming that Nantong Erjian was the main contractor, and Nantong Erjian would charge 1% of the total subcontract price from Hengsen Company as main contractor management fees. The meeting minutes also clarified that the dispute arising from the project delay had been resolved through consultation between the parties. Due to constraints from various factors including the basement causing the project delay, the parties would not pursue the original contract schedule and agreed that there would be neither reward nor penalty. However, the legal representative of Hengsen Company emphasized that the project must be fully completed and ready for acceptance by mid-April 2005.

On April 20, 2005, Nantong Erjian and Hengsen Company signed a supplementary contract, agreeing that Hengsen Company would contract out the general outdoor paving work of the Hengsen International Plaza to Nantong Erjian for construction. The total project price was tentatively set at RMB 2.7 million, and the final settlement price would be confirmed at 12% reduction after audit based on the 2004 Jiangsu Provincial Construction and Installation Quota. The outdoor work工期 was from April 20, 2005, to June 20, 2005.

On June 27, 2005, Nantong Erjian and Hengsen Company held a meeting and signed minutes regarding matters such as the confirmation of on-site project visa orders. The parties confirmed through consultation that the project would be fully completed by the end of June. If it could not be completed on schedule, the responsible party would bear responsibility based on the cause.

During the construction period, Hengsen Company successively subcontracted the plumbing, fire protection, HVAC ventilation, secondary decoration, and curtain wall projects to third parties for construction. Among them, the curtain wall subcontracted project had a fixed total price of RMB 2.05 million. The other four agreements all stipulated that Nantong Erjian would charge the subcontractor coordination management fees at 2.5% of the total subcontract price. It was confirmed that Nantong Erjian had received coordination management fees of RMB 323,750.

The involved project was completed and accepted on July 20, 2005. After project completion, Hengsen Company leased out certain buildings with a total construction area of 22,275 square meters. During the on-site inspection in the original first instance, it was found that the lessee had installed four lighting lamps by drilling screw holes in the center of the roof area.

During the original first instance, Nantong Erjian applied for an audit of the project cost; Hengsen Company applied for an appraisal of the losses from redoing the roof leakage repairs. The court of first instance, upon the parties' applications, commissioned the Suzhou Price Certification Center (hereinafter referred to as the Certification Center), Suzhou Tianzheng Building Safety Judicial Appraisal Institute (hereinafter referred to as Tianzheng Appraisal Institute), and Suzhou Dongwu Architectural Design Institute Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dongwu Design Institute) to appraise the relevant matters.

The appraisal opinion of the Certification Center was: The construction cost of the project constructed by Nantong Erjian was RMB 35,034,260.23, of which the cost for the part actually constructed above the roof structural layer was RMB 1,677,635.

Tianzheng Appraisal Institute determined after appraisal that the roof leakage areas were mainly located at expansion joints, downspouts, roof exhaust pipes, and roof slabs; compared with the original design drawings, the actual construction by Nantong Erjian was missing a 50 mm coarse sand isolation layer, a layer of dry-laid non-woven fabric, a 2.0 mm polymer cement-based elastic waterproof coating layer, and a 20 mm cement mortar leveling layer in the roof waterproof layer construction. Additionally, the expansion joint area was missing a 3.0 mm waterproof membrane. The appraisal opinion was: The roof construction method did not comply with the original design requirements, and the roof leakage range included expansion joints, some downspout pipes, roof exhaust pipes, and some roof slabs.

Dongwu Design Institute clarified in its appraisal that because the existing roof slab construction method did not comply with the original design, a partial repair plan could not ensure a complete and effective resolution of the roof leakage problem (mainly referring to the leakage caused in other parts during partial repair construction). It recommended completely removing the original waterproof layer and redoing the roof waterproof layer, and issued a comprehensive design plan. This comprehensive design plan included work procedures that Nantong Erjian omitted in the actual construction and additionally added an upturned edge at the expansion joint in the original design plan.

The appraisal price issued by the Certification Center based on the above comprehensive design plan of Dongwu Design Institute was RMB 3,975,454 (with April 27, 2009, as the appraisal base date).

During the retrial of the first instance, the court of first instance commissioned the Suzhou Construction Project Quality Testing Center to appraise whether the original design plan's lack of an upturned edge at the expansion joint complied with national and local mandatory standards and whether there was a causal relationship between the installation of four street lamps on the roof and the roof leakage. On March 15, 2012, the Testing Center issued a written appraisal opinion: The expansion joint design style and materials were for reference only and there was no unified mandatory standard. Of the four street lamp bases investigated, three showed no sign of bolt damage to the existing waterproof layer; one street lamp base location showed local damage to the existing waterproof layer, but the degree of impact on the overall waterproof function of the roof waterproof layer could not be clearly determined.

During the retrial of the first instance, the Certification Center issued a summary table, clarifying that among the total repair costs in the comprehensive design plan, the project cost for the unconstructed work procedures in the roof waterproof layer construction method — 50 mm coarse sand isolation layer, a layer of dry-laid non-woven fabric, 2.0 mm polymer cement-based elastic waterproof coating, and 20 mm cement mortar leveling layer — was RMB 755,036.46; the project cost for the unconstructed work procedures at the expansion joint — 50 mm coarse sand isolation layer, a layer of dry-laid non-woven fabric, 2.0 mm polymer cement-based elastic waterproof coating, and 3.0 mm waterproof membrane — was RMB 13,267.56; the project cost for the upturned edge at the expansion joint was RMB 8,713.30.

The court of first instance identified the following issues in dispute:

I. How to determine the project price.

During the proceedings, both Nantong Erjian and Hengsen Company agreed to use the appraised cost of RMB 35,034,260.23 as the basis for the project settlement and both acknowledged that the project款项 already paid was RMB 26,815,307. Nantong Erjian also considered that the project price should additionally include main contractor management fees of RMB 150,000 and losses from成型 steel bars of RMB 60,000.

The court of first instance held that since both parties agreed during the proceedings to use the judicially appraised cost as the basis for the project settlement, this should be permitted. Regarding the main contractor management fees, the parties had confirmed during the construction period that Nantong Erjian was the main contractor and could charge 1% of the total subcontract price from Hengsen Company as main contractor management fees. This was a genuine expression of the parties' intent and should be confirmed. The total subcontract price of Hengsen Company was RMB 15 million, so Hengsen Company should pay RMB 150,000 as agreed. Regarding the losses from成型 steel bars, the parties had agreed that the prerequisite for Hengsen Company to compensate for the loss was that Nantong Erjian submit a detailed list of unusable steel bars. Since Nantong Erjian failed to provide a detailed list of steel bars rendered unusable due to design changes, it should be deemed that those成型 steel bars had been reasonably used in the project, and the constructor had not actually incurred losses from成型 steel bars. Therefore, this claim of Nantong Erjian was not supported. Additionally, since the warranty period had expired and the extensive roof leakage issue would be addressed in this case, Hengsen Company should return the warranty deposit. In summary, the court of first instance determined that the total project price payable by Hengsen Company was RMB 35,184,260.23 (RMB 35,034,260.23 + RMB 150,000). After deducting the project款项 already paid by Hengsen Company (RMB 26,815,307), Hengsen Company still owed Nantong Erjian project price of RMB 8,368,953.23. Interest on the overdue project款项 could be calculated with reference to the payment deadline agreed in the supplementary agreement.

II. Regarding the roof leakage, how should Nantong Erjian, as the construction unit, bear responsibility.

The court of first instance held that, combining the appraisal opinions and the on-site conditions, it should be confirmed that the roof leakage was caused by two factors: Nantong Erjian's failure to construct according to the original design drawings, which created hidden defects, and the lessee's unauthorized installation of street lamps, which damaged the waterproof layer. Among these, failure to construct according to the design drawings was the primary cause, while the street lamp damage to the waterproof layer was a local and secondary cause. Regarding Nantong Erjian's argument that the original design was unreasonable, since the standards or specifications do not have mandatory requirements for an upturned edge at the expansion joint, and there was no other basis to conclude that the lack of an upturned edge at the expansion joint would inevitably cause leakage, this defense was not supported.

Regarding Nantong Erjian's claim that it should only bear warranty obligations, not the comprehensive repair costs, the court of first instance held that because the existing roof slab construction method did not comply with the original design, there were potential quality defects. A partial repair plan could not ensure a complete resolution of the roof leakage problem and would also cause leakage in other areas during the repair construction. Moreover, the quality defects caused by Nantong Erjian's corner-cutting were comprehensive rather than local. Dongwu Design Institute recommended completely removing the original waterproof layer and redoing the roof waterproof layer, and accordingly issued a comprehensive design plan. Compared with the original design plan, this plan only added an upturned edge design at the expansion joint. Therefore, it could be determined that the comprehensive design plan was suitable as a repair plan to completely resolve the roof leakage issue in this case. Given that the two parties had lost their cooperative relationship, it was not feasible for Nantong Erjian to enter the site to redo the waterproof layer. Therefore, Hengsen Company could commission a third party to rectify the roof defects by reference to the comprehensive design plan, and Nantong Erjian should bear the rectification costs.

Regarding how to allocate the comprehensive repair plan cost of RMB 3,975,454, the court of first instance held that compared with the original design, the comprehensive design plan added an upturned edge at the expansion joint. The increased cost of RMB 8,713 should be deducted. The work procedures omitted by Nantong Erjian in the actual construction were not included in the total project price, but the comprehensive design plan included those procedures. Based on the principle of consistency of rights and obligations, this part of the cost should be deducted. However, the roof leakage was mainly caused by Nantong Erjian's construction reasons. At the time of actual repair, labor and material prices in the construction industry had increased, which actually increased Hengsen Company's burden. The increased costs should be borne by Nantong Erjian. According to the appraisal, on October 15, 2004, the actual construction cost for the part of Nantong Erjian's project above the roof structural layer was RMB 1,677,635. On April 27, 2009, the cost for the same quantity of work was RMB 3,198,436.68 (total comprehensive repair cost of RMB 3,975,454 minus the cost of the additional work in the roof waterproof construction method of RMB 755,036.46 minus the cost of the additional work at the expansion joint of RMB 13,267.56 minus the cost of the expansion joint upturned edge of RMB 8,713.30). Therefore, the actual project cost on October 15, 2004, for the work procedures that should have been done but were not done in the roof waterproof construction method and the expansion joint area was RMB 402,988.66. On April 27, 2009, the corresponding project cost was RMB 768,304.02. The difference of RMB 365,315.36 between the two should be borne by Nantong Erjian. Additionally, the lessee's drilling holes on the roof to install lights damaged the waterproof layer, which was also one of the causes of the roof leakage. Therefore, Nantong Erjian's liability should be correspondingly reduced. Given that the streetlight was located at a higher position in the center of the roof parking lot and only affected the roof slab leakage, while the actual leakage areas also included expansion joints, downspouts, roof exhaust pipes, and other parts, the court discretionarily determined to deduct RMB 150,000 from the repair project cost. In summary, the total repair costs payable by Nantong Erjian were RMB 3,413,752.04.

III. Whether Nantong Erjian should bear liability for breach of contract for the delay in project completion.

The court of first instance held that, according to the supplementary agreement, Nantong Erjian should have completed the work by March 11, 2005, or else bear liability for breach of contract at RMB 100,000 per day. During the actual construction period, due to the failure of the foundation works, the parties agreed that Nantong Erjian would take over from the original foundation construction unit to carry out emergency rescue work for the basement enclosure and reinforcement of the retaining piles. This work was not part of the main contractor's contract scope and was an addition to the project, which would necessarily extend the project duration. Therefore, the parties negotiated and agreed not to pursue the original contract schedule, with neither reward nor penalty. However, Hengsen Company did not waive its requirements regarding the completion date. While promising not to impose penalties or rewards based on the original schedule, it required that Nantong Erjian must complete the work by mid-April 2005. Furthermore, Hengsen Company separately contracted the outdoor paving work to Nantong Erjian and expressly set the outdoor work completion date as June 20, 2005. Combined with the parties' expression of intent in the meeting minutes of June 27, 2005, that the project should be completed by the end of June or else the responsible party would bear responsibility based on the cause, it could be considered that the parties had, due to reasons including the basement and increased work volume, negotiated to extend the completion date to June 30, 2005. In fact, the project was completed on July 20, 2005. Nantong Erjian was 20 days late in completion. Nantong Erjian failed to provide evidence that these 20 days were subject to any excusable extension. Therefore, Nantong Erjian should bear responsibility for the 20-day delay. Since one of Hengsen Company's purposes for investing in the construction was to lease the property to large stores to obtain rental income, Nantong Erjian's delay in completion would inevitably cause Hengsen Company to receive and use the property later and obtain rental income later. Considering the actual leasing situation and scale of Hengsen Company's constructed property, the court of first instance discretionarily determined that Nantong Erjian should compensate for the loss due to the delay in the amount of RMB 250,000.

In summary, the court of first instance, in accordance with Articles 77, 107, and 281 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 14, 17, and 18 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Construction Project Construction Contracts, Article 13 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2007), and Articles 2 and 71 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, rendered the following judgment on August 31, 2012:

1. Hengsen Company shall pay Nantong Erjian the project price of RMB 8,368,953.23.
2. Hengsen Company shall pay Nantong Erjian interest on the remaining project款项.
3. Nantong Erjian shall compensate Hengsen Company for roof repair costs of RMB 3,413,752.04.
4. Nantong Erjian shall compensate Hengsen Company for losses due to project delay of RMB 250,000.
5. The other claims of Nantong Erjian and Hengsen Company are dismissed.

Nantong Second Construction appealed the first-instance judgment to the Jiangsu High People's Court, alleging: 1. The project in question had passed completion inspection and acceptance, and the construction unit should only be liable for warranty repair. The first-instance court's decision requiring Nantong Second Construction to bear the cost of complete roof reconstruction lacked legal basis. 2. The original design was defective, which also contributed to the roof leakage, and the first-instance court erred in not determining the liability for the original design defects. 3. The contract between the parties stipulated a 9.5% downward adjustment of the total project price, so the repair costs should also be subject to a 9.5% downward adjustment. 4. The 0-100 thick C30 fine stone concrete leveling layer was an additional process added to coordinate with the expansion joint flashing; this process was not in the original design, so its cost should be deducted. 5. The first-instance court found that, among the causes of the roof leakage, damage to the waterproof layer by street lamps was a secondary cause. Reducing Nantong Second Construction's liability by only RMB 150,000 was unfair. In summary, it requested a judgment according to law.

The appellee, Hengsen Company, argued in its defense: 1. Nantong Second Construction's argument that the project had passed inspection and acceptance and therefore it should only bear warranty obligations was untenable, because the roof leakage was caused by Nantong Second Construction's unauthorized reduction of construction processes. Complete reconstruction was necessary to effectively resolve the leakage, and Nantong Second Construction should bear full compensation liability. 2. The downward adjustment of the project cost for the actually constructed portion was based on the parties' agreement in the construction contract. However, the engineering cost of the comprehensive design plan was the compensation liability that Nantong Second Construction, as the constructor, owed to Hengsen Company, and should not be adjusted downward. 3. The cost of the 0-100 thick C30 fine stone concrete leveling layer should not be deducted, because the comprehensive design plan was designed to completely resolve the roof leakage, and the roof leakage was caused by Nantong Second Construction's failure to construct according to the design. Therefore, no costs from the comprehensive design plan should be deducted. It requested that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed.

The Jiangsu High People's Court found the facts to be the same as those found by the first-instance court.

The court of second instance additionally found: The appraisal personnel of Dongwu Design Institute stated during the second-instance trial that the original design of the project did not include the 0-100 mm thick fine stone concrete leveling layer process; this process was added to coordinate with the flashing design at the expansion joints. The total cost for this portion amounted to RMB 536,379.74. As confirmed by both parties, the issues in dispute at second instance were: 1. Whether there were design-related causes for the roof leakage quality problem; what repair plan should be adopted for the roof leakage quality problem. 2. If the repair was to be carried out according to the comprehensive design plan, how should the costs of the comprehensive design plan be apportioned; should the costs of the comprehensive design plan be subject to a 9.5% downward adjustment; and should the cost of the 0-100 mm thick fine stone concrete leveling layer in the comprehensive design plan be deducted.

The Jiangsu High People's Court held in its second-instance judgment:

I. The widespread roof leakage was an objective fact that had been confirmed by the court. The certificate of completion inspection and acceptance and any other written documents could not effectively contradict this objective fact. Therefore, Nantong Second Construction's defense against the widespread roof leakage based on the certificate of acceptance was untenable. Its argument, based on the *Regulations on the Administration of Construction Project Quality*, that it should only bear warranty liability and not be required to reconstruct, was also untenable. This was because the *Regulations* are administrative norms, while the roof leakage in this case was mainly caused by the use of inferior materials and cutting corners by Nantong Second Construction during the construction process. The roof it delivered itself did not comply with the contract requirements and had caused damage to Hengsen Company that could not be remedied by mere warranty repair. Therefore, the basic legal basis for the judgment in this case was the *General Principles of the Civil Law*, the *Contract Law*, and other basic laws, not the *Regulations*. According to the hierarchy of legal norms, the *Regulations* were only for reference in this case. The liability for compensation for the roof leakage quality problem in this case should be handled according to the principle of "who causes the harm bears the responsibility," which conforms to the principle of fairness under the law.

II. The quality problem of the roof leakage was not due to the original design but to Nantong Second Construction's use of inferior materials and failure to construct according to the design requirements. Therefore, repair should be carried out according to the comprehensive design plan. Nantong Second Construction appealed, arguing that the original design's expansion joints lacked a flashing design, which did not comply with the requirements of the Su J9503 drawing set; that the roof expansion joints in the original design did not span the low points of the roof valley, and the designed slope was insufficient; and that the roof expansion joints in the original design bonded two incompatible materials. It claimed that these design defects were all causes of the roof leakage. Regarding the objections raised by Nantong Second Construction, the Engineering Quality Testing Center had previously issued an appraisal opinion on March 15, 2012, explaining whether the original design was defective and whether there was a causal relationship with the roof leakage. During the second-instance trial, the appraisal personnel of the Engineering Quality Testing Center also appeared in court and were examined. Regarding the issue of the expansion joints lacking a flashing design in the original design, the second-instance court held that the Su J9503 drawing set was not a mandatory requirement. Adding flashing to expansion joints was merely a more effective waterproofing measure for further certainty. There was no necessary connection between whether expansion joints had flashing and roof leakage. If the constructor had constructed according to the original design specifications with guaranteed quality, combined with general engineering construction practice, the roof would not have leaked. Nantong Second Construction's ground of appeal seeking to reduce its own liability by arguing that the original design's expansion joints lacked a flashing design lacked a basis. Regarding the issue that the original design's roof expansion joints did not span the low points of the roof valley, the second-instance court held that increasing the roof slope and spanning the low points of the valley, while beneficial for waterproofing and leakage prevention, would not have prevented leakage if Nantong Second Construction had strictly constructed according to the original design standards. Therefore, this ground of appeal by Nantong Second Construction was also untenable. Regarding the issue that the original design bonded two incompatible materials at the roof expansion joints, the second-instance court held that different materials are inherently difficult to be perfectly compatible, and there are no relevant national regulations or standards prohibiting the bonding of such materials. This point also had no necessary connection with the roof leakage. Therefore, this ground of appeal by Nantong Second Construction was also untenable. Furthermore, both parties to a contract should earnestly and in good faith attend to the realization of the other party's rights during the performance of the contract. This is both a collateral obligation of the contract and closely related to the realization of one's own rights. Therefore, Nantong Second Construction's defenses of this nature should have been raised through communication beforehand, rather than serving as sufficient grounds to shift its responsibility.

Regarding the issue of which repair plan should be adopted for the roof leakage in this case, the second-instance court held that, according to Articles 107 and 281 of the *Contract Law of the People's Republic of China*, if the quality of a project fails to meet the contractual requirements due to the constructor's reasons, the constructor should bear the liability for breach of contract, including making free repairs, reworking, reconstructing, or compensating for losses. In this case, the parties clearly stipulated the construction processes for the roof in question. However, during the construction process, Nantong Second Construction unilaterally reduced multiple processes, especially omitting the 2.0 thick polymer cement-based elastic waterproof coating layer, which was crucial for waterproofing. The roof it delivered did not meet the contractual requirements, causing the roof leakage, for which it should bear liability for breach of contract. Given that Hengsen Company had carried out several local repairs but could still not completely resolve the roof leakage, and the parties had lost the cooperative foundation of trust, in order to completely resolve the dispute between the parties, the first-instance court's decision, based on the judicial appraisal opinion, to adopt the comprehensive design plan for repair, and its judgment that Hengsen Company should entrust a third party to rectify the roof leakage according to the comprehensive design plan, with Nantong Second Construction bearing the corresponding liability for the reconstruction, had factual and legal basis and was also necessary.

III. The repair costs under the comprehensive design plan should be reasonably apportioned based on the actual circumstances of the case. The second-instance court held that, when determining compensation liability, the various causes of the damage and the relative strength of each cause should be the guiding principle. The first-instance court, based on the appraisal opinions of Tianzheng Appraisal Institute and the Engineering Quality Testing Center, found that Nantong Second Construction's failure to construct according to the design drawings was the primary cause of the roof leakage, while the damage to the waterproof layer by street lamps was a local and secondary cause. Given that the appraisal institution could not make a clear determination of the impact of the street lamp damage on the overall waterproofing function of the roof waterproof layer, and considering factors such as the relationship between the leakage locations and the street lamp locations, the degree of influence of the local damage to the waterproof layer by the street lamps on the overall roof leakage situation, and the fact that Nantong Second Construction had unilaterally reduced processes first, making it difficult to avoid the roof leakage even without the holes from the street lamp bolts affecting the waterproof layer, the first-instance court's discretionary reduction of Nantong Second Construction's liability by RMB 150,000 was appropriate. As for whether the costs of the comprehensive design plan should be subject to a 9.5% downward adjustment, the second-instance court held that bearing the engineering cost of the comprehensive design plan was the liability for breach of contract that Nantong Second Construction, as the constructor, owed to Hengsen Company. This is a different legal relationship from the settlement of the actual construction project costs. Nantong Second Construction's request to calculate the repair costs of the comprehensive design plan by applying the 9.5% downward adjustment used for the construction project costs lacked both a contractual and a legal basis. Regarding whether the cost of the 0-100 mm thick fine stone concrete leveling layer, amounting to RMB 536,379.74, should be deducted from the comprehensive design plan costs, the second-instance court held that the 0-100 mm thick fine stone concrete leveling layer was not in the original design of the project in question; it was an addition in the comprehensive design plan to coordinate with the flashing design at the expansion joints. Therefore, the increased cost of RMB 536,379.74 should be deducted from the total repair costs. Based on the foregoing, the total repair costs payable by Nantong Second Construction in this case were RMB 2,877,372.30 (RMB 3,198,436.68 + RMB 365,315.36 - RMB 150,000 - RMB 536,379.74).

In conclusion, the Jiangsu High People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) (as amended in 2007) of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, rendered the following judgment on December 15, 2012:

Items 1, 2, 4, and 5 of the main text of the first-instance judgment were affirmed. Item 3 of the main text of the first-instance judgment was modified to: Nantong Second Construction shall compensate Hengsen Company for roof repair costs in the amount of RMB 2,877,372.30.

This judgment is final.
